</span><button tabindex="0" style="margin: 0px 6px 0px 0px; background-color: var(--aYn2S); border: none; border-radius: 10px; height: 20px; padding: 0px; width: 20px; outline: 0px; cursor: pointer;"><span style="color: var(--IXoxUe); display: inline-block; transform: rotate(135deg);"><svg style="margin-top: 3px;" fill="currentColor" width="12px" height="12px" focusable="false" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M3.9 12c0-1.71 1.39-3.1 3.1-3.1h4V7H7c-2.76 0-5 2.24-5 5s2.24 5 5 5h4v-1.9H7c-1.71 0-3.1-1.39-3.1-3.1zM8 13h8v-2H8v2zm9-6h-4v1.9h4c1.71 0 3.1 1.39 3.1 3.1s-1.39 3.1-3.1 3.1h-4V17h4c2.76 0 5-2.24 5-5s-2.24-5-5-5z"></path></svg></span></button></span></span></div><div style="-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; font-family: &quot;Google Sans&quot;, &quot;Helvetica Neue&quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 400; line-height: 24px; letter-spacing: 0px; overflow-wrap: break-word; margin-block: var(--NxiBJE--LYjWYD,12px) var(--NxiBJE--akGBcD,16px);">In technology,<span> </span><strong style="font-weight: 700;">CSS
</strong>
<span>
 </span>is a stylesheet language used to describe the visual presentation of documents written in HTML or XML. It is a core technology of the World Wide Web alongside HTML and JavaScript.<span><span style="white-space: nowrap; position: relative;">
<span>
 </span><button tabindex="0" style="margin: 0px 6px 0px 0px; background-color: var(--aYn2S); border: none; border-radius: 10px; height: 20px; padding: 0px; width: 20px; outline: 0px; cursor: pointer;"><span style="color: var(--IXoxUe); display: inline-block; transform: rotate(135deg);"><svg style="margin-top: 3px;" fill="currentColor" width="12px" height="12px" focusable="false" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M3.9 12c0-1.71 1.39-3.1 3.1-3.1h4V7H7c-2.76 0-5 2.24-5 5s2.24 5 5 5h4v-1.9H7c-1.71 0-3.1-1.39-3.1-3.1zM8 13h8v-2H8v2zm9-6h-4v1.9h4c1.71 0 3.1 1.39 3.1 3.1s-1.39 3.1-3.1 3.1h-4V17h4c2.76 0 5-2.24 5-5s-2.24-5-5-5z"></path></svg></span></button></span></span></div><ul style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px; margin-block: 12px 16px; font-family: &quot;Google Sans&quot;, &quot;Helvetica Neue&quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 400; line-height: 24px; letter-spacing: 0px; padding-inline-start: 16px;"><li style="margin: 0px 0px 12px; padding: 0px; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; list-style: disc; padding-inline-start: 4px;"><span style="overflow-wrap: break-word;"><strong style="font-weight: 700;">Function:
</strong>
<span>
 </span>It controls layout, colors, fonts, and overall design to separate content (HTML) from presentation.</span></li><li style="margin: 0px 0px 12px; padding: 0px; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; list-style: disc; padding-inline-start: 4px;"><span style="overflow-wrap: break-word;"><strong style="font-weight: 700;">Syntax:
</strong>
<span>
 </span>A CSS rule consists of a<span> </span><strong style="font-weight: 700;">selector
</strong>
<span>
 </span>(the HTML element to style) and a<span> </span><strong style="font-weight: 700;">declaration block
</strong>
<span>
 </span>containing properties and values (e.g.,<span> </span><code style="font-size: 14px; line-height: 22px; background-color: var(--XKMDxc); border: 1px solid var(--XKMDxc); border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 4px;">color: blue;</code>).</span></li><li style="margin: 0px 0px 12px; padding: 0px; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; list-style: disc; padding-inline-start: 4px;"><span style="overflow-wrap: break-word;"><strong style="font-weight: 700;">Implementation:
</strong>
<span>
 </span>It can be added to web pages in three ways:<span> </span><strong style="font-weight: 700;">Inline
</strong>
<span>
 </span>(within HTML tags),<span> </span><strong style="font-weight: 700;">Internal
</strong>
<span>
 </span>(inside a<span> </span><code style="font-size: 14px; line-height: 22px; background-color: var(--XKMDxc); border: 1px solid var(--XKMDxc); border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 4px;">&lt;style&gt;
</code>
<span>
 </span>block), or<span> </span><strong style="font-weight: 700;">External</strong><div tabindex="0" style="outline: 0px; border: 0px; clip: rect(0px, 0px, 0px, 0px); clip-path: polygon(0px 0px, 0px 0px, 0px 0px); height: 1px; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; overflow: auto;  overflow: auto;  padding: 0px; position: absolute; width: 1px; white-space: nowrap; appearance: none; z-index: -1000;"></div><div tabindex="0" style="outline: 0px; border: 0px; clip: rect(0px, 0px, 0px, 0px); clip-path: polygon(0px 0px, 0px 0px, 0px 0px); height: 1px; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; overflow: auto;  overflow: auto;  padding: 0px; position: absolute; width: 1px; white-space: nowrap; appearance: none; z-index: -1000;">
</div>
<span>
 </span>(via a separate<span> </span><code style="font-size: 14px; line-height: 22px; background-color: var(--XKMDxc); border: 1px solid var(--XKMDxc); border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 4px;">.css
</code>
<span>
 </span>file linked to the HTML).</span></li><li style="margin: 0px 0px 12px; padding: 0px; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; list-style: disc; padding-inline-start: 4px;"><span style="overflow-wrap: break-word;"><strong style="font-weight: 700;">Evolution:
</strong>
<span>
 </span>As of 2025, CSS is no longer versioned as a single monolithic block (like "CSS3"). Instead, it is developed in independent modules (e.g., Selectors Level 4), which the W3C periodically collects into<span> </span><strong style="font-weight: 700;">Snapshots
</strong>
<span>
 </span>to define the current state of the language.
</span>
<span>

</strong>
<span>
 </span>is an online application administered by the<span> </span><strong style="font-weight: 700;">College Board</strong>.<span><span style="white-space: nowrap; position: relative;">
<span>
 </span><button tabindex="0" style="margin: 0px 6px 0px 0px; background-color: var(--aYn2S); border: none; border-radius: 10px; height: 20px; padding: 0px; width: 20px; outline: 0px; cursor: pointer;"><span style="color: var(--IXoxUe); display: inline-block; transform: rotate(135deg);"><svg style="margin-top: 3px;" fill="currentColor" width="12px" height="12px" focusable="false" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M3.9 12c0-1.71 1.39-3.1 3.1-3.1h4V7H7c-2.76 0-5 2.24-5 5s2.24 5 5 5h4v-1.9H7c-1.71 0-3.1-1.39-3.1-3.1zM8 13h8v-2H8v2zm9-6h-4v1.9h4c1.71 0 3.1 1.39 3.1 3.1s-1.39 3.1-3.1 3.1h-4V17h4c2.76 0 5-2.24 5-5s-2.24-5-5-5z"></path></svg></span></button></span></span></div><ul style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px; margin-block: 12px 16px; font-family: &quot;Google Sans&quot;, &quot;Helvetica Neue&quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 400; line-height: 24px; letter-spacing: 0px; padding-inline-start: 16px;"><li style="margin: 0px 0px 12px; padding: 0px; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; list-style: disc; padding-inline-start: 4px;"><span style="overflow-wrap: break-word;"><strong style="font-weight: 700;">Purpose:
</strong>
<span>
 </span>It is used by nearly 400 colleges, universities, and scholarship programs to award non-federal institutional financial aid.</span></li><li style="margin: 0px 0px 12px; padding: 0px; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; list-style: disc; padding-inline-start: 4px;"><span style="overflow-wrap: break-word;"><strong style="font-weight: 700;">Requirement:
</strong>
<span>
 </span>Unlike the FAFSA (which is for federal aid), the CSS Profile is often required by private institutions to gain a deeper understanding of a family's financial situation.</span></li><li style="margin: 0px 0px 12px; padding: 0px; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; list-style: disc; padding-inline-start: 4px;"><span style="overflow-wrap: break-word;"><strong style="font-weight: 700;">Deadlines:
</strong>

For a publication focused on art and aesthetics, these designs prioritize white space, asymmetrical layouts, and high-quality photography</div>.
</div>
<div style="margin-block: 24px 12px; font-family: &quot;Google Sans&quot;, &quot;Helvetica Neue&quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 20px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 28px; letter-spacing: 0px; color: var(--jINu6c);">Slick Design Examples for Modern Periodicals</div><ul style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px; margin-block: 12px 16px; font-family: &quot;Google Sans&quot;, &quot;Helvetica Neue&quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 400; line-height: 24px; letter-spacing: 0px; padding-inline-start: 16px;"><li style="margin: 0px 0px 12px; padding: 0px; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; list-style: disc; padding-inline-start: 4px;"><span style="overflow-wrap: break-word;"><strong style="font-weight: 700;">Swiss Brutalist Approach:
</strong>
<span>
 </span>This style uses a strict grid with heavy, sans-serif typography. A thin, vibrant linear gradient under the subheading (<code style="font-size: 14px; line-height: 22px; background-color: var(--XKMDxc); border: 1px solid var(--XKMDxc); border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 4px;">h2</code>) provides a sharp contrast against a monochromatic or brutalist layout.</span></li><li style="margin: 0px 0px 12px; padding: 0px; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; list-style: disc; padding-inline-start: 4px;"><span style="overflow-wrap: break-word;"><strong style="font-weight: 700;">Minimalist Gallery Aesthetic:
</strong>
<span>
 </span>Focus on extreme white space and centered text containers. A subtle "fading" gradient border on the<span> </span><code style="font-size: 14px; line-height: 22px; background-color: var(--XKMDxc); border: 1px solid var(--XKMDxc); border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 4px;">h2
</code>
<span>
 </span>can act as a divider that guides the eye without cluttering the page.</span></li><li style="margin: 0px 0px 12px; padding: 0px; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; list-style: disc; padding-inline-start: 4px;"><span style="overflow-wrap: break-word;"><strong style="font-weight: 700;">The "Digital Glossy" Spread:
</strong>
<span>
 </span>Inspired by high-end fashion magazines, this uses asymmetric CSS grids where text might flow around images. Use a thick, bold gradient border to ground the<span> </span><code style="font-size: 14px; line-height: 22px; background-color: var(--XKMDxc); border: 1px solid var(--XKMDxc); border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 4px;">h2
</code>
<span>
 </span>and signify the start of a deep-dive essay.</span></li><li style="margin: 0px 0px 12px; padding: 0px; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; list-style: disc; padding-inline-start: 4px;"><span style="overflow-wrap: break-word;"><strong style="font-weight: 700;">Experimental Typography:
</strong>
<span>
 </span>For publications that treat the website itself as art, you can use "text-as-shape" where the<span> </span><code style="font-size: 14px; line-height: 22px; background-color: var(--XKMDxc); border: 1px solid var(--XKMDxc); border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 4px;">h1
</code>
<span>
 </span>and<span> </span><code style="font-size: 14px; line-height: 22px; background-color: var(--XKMDxc); border: 1px solid var(--XKMDxc); border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 4px;">h2
</code>
<span>
 </span>are oversized and overlapping, with the gradient border serving as an architectural element.</span></li>
</ul>

</strong>
<span>
 </span>Liquid-glass designs can sometimes reduce text legibility due to transparency. Ensure your<span> </span><code style="font-size: 14px; line-height: 22px; background-color: var(--XKMDxc); border: 1px solid var(--XKMDxc); border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 4px;">h2
</code>
<span>
 </span>text has a high enough contrast (e.g., a dark color on a light frosted background).</span></li><li style="margin: 0px 0px 12px; padding: 0px; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; list-style: disc; padding-inline-start: 4px;"><span style="overflow-wrap: break-word;"><strong style="font-weight: 700;">Performance:
</strong>
<span>
 </span>Effects like<span> </span><code style="font-size: 14px; line-height: 22px; background-color: var(--XKMDxc); border: 1px solid var(--XKMDxc); border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 4px;">backdrop-filter: blur()
</code>
<span>
 </span>can be resource-heavy on older mobile devices. Apply them selectively to key headers rather than every element.</span></li><li style="margin: 0px 0px 12px; padding: 0px; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; list-style: disc; padding-inline-start: 4px;"><span style="overflow-wrap: break-word;"><strong style="font-weight: 700;">Context-Awareness:
</strong>
<span>
 </span>In the 2025 "Liquid Glass" philosophy, the UI should adapt to the background. Use<span> </span><code style="font-size: 14px; line-height: 22px; background-color: var(--XKMDxc); border: 1px solid var(--XKMDxc); border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 4px;">rgba()
</code>
<span>
 </span>colors so your glass effect inherits the hues of the art photography beneath it.</span></li>
</ul>
